subject.title: [Bug]: Memory dreaming narrative/REM lane is given apply_patch and misuses it

question: Should plugin subagent runs gain an explicit no-tools or runtime allowlist contract, and should memory-core Dream Diary narratives use it with an empty or minimal tool set?
rationale: The useful fix crosses plugin SDK, Gateway protocol, agent runtime, and security-boundary semantics; automation should not invent that public/internal contract without maintainer direction.

options.title: Add subagent tool scoping
options.body: Extend the plugin subagent API and Gateway agent path with a typed no-tools or `toolsAllow` contract, then set the Dream Diary narrative lane to a prose-only tool profile.

options.title: Prompt-only mitigation
options.body: Tighten the narrative prompt only, which may reduce bad model behavior but leaves the mutating tool exposed and does not solve the security boundary.

options.title: Defer as low-impact noise
options.body: Accept the current fallback log noise and keep the lane unchanged until a broader plugin subagent policy redesign is scheduled.

recommendation.title: Add subagent tool scoping
recommendation.body: Extend the plugin subagent API and Gateway agent path with a typed no-tools or `toolsAllow` contract, then set the Dream Diary narrative lane to a prose-only tool profile.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties this handle to the plugin runtime, Gateway bridge, and embedded tool-construction surfaces that would define the contract.
